hooks.name: Generate architecture diagram when agent changes
hooks.description: When any of agent.py, decision.py, tools.py, or AGENT.md changes, regenerate docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with an up-to-date Mermaid architecture diagram showing the full agent flow: citizen → gate → Strands Decider 2B → verdict branches → Strands Agent / tools → response.

action.prompt:
The file just saved is part of the agent. Read the current state of these files before doing anything:
- agent/AGENT.md  (use case, pitch, features, decision rationale)
- agent/agent.py  (HackathonAgent, tools list, Strands Agent wiring)
- agent/decision.py (PATTERN_TAG, QUESTIONS, the gate/wiring class)
- agent/tools.py  (all @tool functions the agent can call)

Then create or overwrite docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with a clean architecture diagram for this agent using Mermaid flowchart syntax (top-down). The diagram MUST show all of the following as distinct nodes:

1. Citizen / User (entry point)
2. HackathonAgent.chat() (agent/agent.py)
3. SchemeEligibilityGate (or whatever the gate class is in agent/decision.py) — labelled with PATTERN_TAG
4. Strands Decider 2B — the decision model
5. The three verdict branches: allow / review / block — each as a separate path
6. Block path: returns refusal reply directly (no LLM, no tools called)
7. Review path: injects caution note into system prompt, then continues to the Strands Agent
8. Allow path: continues directly to the Strands Agent
9. Strands Agent (LLM via Amazon Bedrock — model from BEDROCK_MODEL_ID env var, default Nova Pro)
10. Each tool defined in agent/tools.py — as individual nodes grouped under a "Tools" subgraph
11. Response returned to citizen

Also add a second smaller diagram (Mermaid graph LR) showing the deployment topology:
- Demo UI (demo/server.py, port 8501)
- HackathonAgent
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime (deployed via ./kit deploy)
- Strands Decider 2B (local GPU / hosted API / UGMDU cloud — read DECIDER_MODE from .env context)
- Amazon Polly (used by scripts/record_video.py for narration)

Rules for the file:
- Use only Mermaid code blocks (```mermaid). No external image links.
- Add a one-paragraph prose summary above the diagrams that explains the flow in plain English: what happens before the LLM runs, what the decider decides, and what the three branches do.
- Include the agent name (from NAME in agent/agent.py) as the H1 heading.
- End the file with: "Generated by the architecture-diagram hook. Built with the AWS User Group Madurai Strands Decider hackathon kit."
- Keep the diagram accurate to the actual code — do not invent components. If a tool is removed from agent/tools.py, remove it from the diagram.
- Do not modify any file other than docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
